note: Scripture authority is the Open Word Bible (OWB), Amharic, Balanced edition (CC0), read offline from the bundled owb-am text, per the founder decision of 2026-11-18 that every Amharic work quotes OWB. Every quotation was re-quoted to it verbatim, replacing the 1962 UBS wording and the OT renderings made in its register: Evans's recitations of Isaiah 40:28-31 and Psalm 103:1-5, his cited verses, the gift lists of Ephesians 4, Romans 12 and 1 Corinthians 12, and the phrases he returns to ('equip the saints', 'apt to teach', 'my yoke is easy and my burden is light').

A `mined` row is a verbatim OWB span in that block: the whole verse or range, the shortest span carrying the quoted clause, or exact OWB pieces joined with '…'. Where OWB opens an inner quotation inside a verse, the inner marks are ‹ ›. `self_rendered` rows (each with a `why`) are allusions, the author's own paraphrases and dramatised retellings, and his reading of the Greek.

Judgement calls. Ephesians 4:12 'equip the saints for the work of ministry' is OWB «የእግዚአብሔርን ቅዱስ ሕዝብ ለአገልግሎት ሥራ ለማዘጋጀት», used everywhere Evans recites it, marked or not. 1 Timothy 3:2 'apt to teach' is OWB «ማስተማር የሚችል». Matthew 11:30's 'easy' and 'light' are OWB «ምቹ» and «ቀላል»; the author's prose and the Q&A that argue from them follow (ልዝብ/ቀሊል → ምቹ/ቀላል). Isaiah 40:31 'mount up with wings as eagles' is OWB «ክንፋቸውን ዘርግተው እንደ ንስሮች ከፍ ብለው ይወጣሉ», and the book Q&A follows. Numbers 4:15 'the burden of the sons of Kohath' is OWB «ቀዓታውያን የሚሸከሟቸው…» ('what the Kohathites carry'), which keeps the carrying David's chapter turns on. Luke 24:49 OWB says «በዚህ ከተማ» where the English names Jerusalem. Romans 12:10 was miscited as 12:19 in the Amharic; the citation now reads 12:10. Ephesians 5:18 «ዘወትር መንፈስ ይሙላባችሁ» stays the translator's: Evans argues from the Greek present tense ('keep on being filled'), which OWB's «መንፈስ ይሙላችሁ» does not carry. Christ's prayer in John 17 is adapted by the author ('all those in (your church, your city)'); that sentence stays his, and vv. 21-23 after it are OWB. The 'gates of hell' allusions in Evans's own sentences keep the translator's wording; the one place he quotes Matthew 16:18 is OWB.
